findings.claim: Any caller can issue credit to any target account because actor_account_id is never checked, allowing unauthorized financial balance changes.
evidence: In src/credits.py:16-26, issue_credit accepts actor_account_id but never reads it and unconditionally calls ledger.add with target_account_id after only validating that the amount is positive.
A runtime call with actor_account_id='acct-attacker' and target_account_id='acct-victim' succeeded and appended a 2500-cent credit for acct-victim.
tests/test_credits.py:4-16 covers only actor_account_id equal to target_account_id, so it does not exercise or reject cross-account issuance.

findings.claim: Retries with the same request_id create duplicate credits, so a client or transport retry can credit an account multiple times for one logical request.
evidence: In src/credits.py:5-13, CreditLedger.add stores request_id but performs no lookup or uniqueness check before appending a new entry.
Two runtime calls using the same actor, target, amount, and request_id='req-retry' returned distinct entry IDs 2 and 3 and both remained in the ledger.
tests/test_credits.py contains only one issue_credit call and has no replay or duplicate-request assertion.

uncertainties: The case does not define which actors, if any, should be authorized to issue cross-account credits; however, the complete absence of any use of actor_account_id means no authorization policy can be enforced by this operation.
The case does not specify whether CreditLedger is shared across threads or processes, so concurrency and durability risks of its in-memory list were not elevated to separate findings.
